steps.path: Appears when you open the app after it closed with sessions open
steps.headline: The contract, graded — accept these verdicts?

rows.statement: Only sessions where you sent at least one message appear on the Welcome back screen.
rows.threshold: empty sessions are excluded, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Closing the app with sessions open lets you choose, with a toggle, whether they come back next launch.
rows.threshold: toggle is present and controls reopening, confirmed in a dev instance
rows.note: "Reopen on next launch?" with toggle, otherwise all crashes/unexpected exits

rows.statement: Closing a session with its X removes it from Welcome back for good; it stays in the Resume browser.
rows.threshold: X'd sessions never reappear on Welcome back, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Each computer only offers back the sessions that were open on that same computer.
rows.threshold: a session open elsewhere doesn't appear on this computer's Welcome back, confirmed with two devices

rows.statement: Opening the app after it closed with sessions open shows a full Welcome back screen instead of the start screen.
rows.threshold: Welcome back replaces the start screen until you choose, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Every session on the Welcome back list starts ticked, ready to resume.
rows.threshold: all rows start ticked on open, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Each session row on Welcome back has a Mark complete button, meaning the same as in the Resume browser.
rows.threshold: Mark complete hides the row there and in the Resume browser, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Sessions you leave unticked are forgotten; they won't reappear on Welcome back next launch.
rows.threshold: unticked rows are gone next launch but still in the Resume browser, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Resuming a session from Welcome back reuses its last model automatically instead of asking which one to use.
rows.threshold: no model picker appears when the model is available, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: This ships on the desktop app first; nothing changes on the Android app.
rows.threshold: no Android-facing changes shipped with this feature

rows.statement: Each session's tags and folder line sit under its name, not under the tick box.
rows.threshold: matches the approved picture, re-shot from the built branch
rows.evidence: Re-shot http://127.0.0.1:5260/?mode=workbench&child=1&view=app&scenario=welcome-back at 1440x900 (scratch/grader/r11-r17-welcome-back.png) vs approved docs/active/design/2026-09-24-welcome-back/images/welcome-back.review-2/stacked--midnight--after.png: every row's tags (e.g. Priority/bug, idea/work) and folder/model/size/date line sit under the session name, to the right of the tick box, matching the approved picture exactly.

rows.statement: That reopen tick box starts unticked, so quitting without touching it does not bring sessions back.
rows.threshold: toggle is off by default, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: A crash, power loss, shutdown, restart, or quitting from the menu always brings your sessions back.
rows.threshold: sessions return after each of these closing methods, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: The Welcome back screen has no search box, filters, or 'Show complete' switch.
rows.threshold: none of those controls appear on the built screen

rows.statement: Escape and clicking outside do nothing on Welcome back; it closes itself once every row is resumed.
rows.threshold: Escape/outside click don't dismiss it, and it auto-closes when empty, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Resume and Start fresh appear as two full-width, stacked buttons, like the app's other pop-ups.
rows.threshold: matches the approved 'stacked' picture, re-shot from the built branch
rows.evidence: Same re-shot (scratch/grader/r11-r17-welcome-back.png) vs approved docs/active/design/2026-09-24-welcome-back/images/welcome-back.review-2/stacked--midnight--after.png: 'Resume all 4' and 'Start fresh' render as two full-width buttons stacked vertically, identical layout to the approved 'stacked' variant chosen in review-2 (C-1, pick: stacked).

rows.statement: The quit warning's reopen switch is labeled 'Resume on Next Launch?'; the window itself keeps the plainer title 'Close window'.
rows.threshold: switch label and window title match, checked against the built branch

rows.statement: A bold header line above the quit warning's message states how many sessions are open and asks 'proceed?'.
rows.threshold: header text matches, checked against the built branch

rows.statement: The quit warning's body says closing ends your sessions and asks if you want the option to resume them next launch.
rows.threshold: body text matches, checked against the built branch

rows.statement: The reopen toggle sits in line with the Close window button, even if the window has to widen.
rows.threshold: toggle and button share a row, checked against the built branch

rows.statement: Resuming a session always defaults to its last model; only Welcome back skips the click needed to confirm it.
rows.threshold: confirmed by resuming from both surfaces in a dev instance

rows.statement: Welcome back lets you preview, tag, add notes to, rename and complete each session before reopening it, like the Resume browser.
rows.threshold: each action available on Welcome back rows, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: The quit warning is a YouCoded window styled like 'Close session,' not your computer's own pop-up.
rows.threshold: quit warning renders as an in-app window, confirmed in a dev instance

rows.statement: Handing off a Claude Code session to another device removes it from this device's Welcome back, same as a native session.
rows.threshold: both pinned-snapshot Claude Code untrack tests pass
rows.evidence: npx vitest run tests/holder-takeover.test.ts (youcoded/desktop) — 29 passed, incl. both pinned-snapshot Claude Code untrack tests ('pinned-snapshot path: untracks Welcome back for a Claude Code writer once stop is proven' and '...even when the stop is unproven'); read takeover.ts:155-163 — the else-if (provider === 'claude') branch now calls deps.untrackWelcomeBack?.(id) unconditionally, matching the native branch.

rows.statement: A resume that fails removes the session from Welcome back instead of leaving it stuck as still open.
rows.threshold: the failed-native-resume untrack test passes
rows.evidence: npx vitest run tests/ipc-handlers.test.ts (youcoded/desktop) — 49 passed, incl. 'rejects and tears down a resumed id without a native harness' which asserts welcomeBackStore.untrack toHaveBeenCalledWith('ghost-native-1') after a failed native resume; read ipc-handlers.ts:1008-1024 — the catch block's successful-teardown path now calls untrackWelcomeBack(info.id) when opts.resumeSessionId is set.

rows.statement: Opening a session's tag/notes editor on Welcome back scrolls that row into view instead of hiding it behind the buttons.
rows.threshold: the Organize-sheet scroll-into-view test passes
rows.evidence: npx vitest run tests/ResumeBrowser-welcome-back.test.tsx (youcoded/desktop) — 19 passed, incl. "opening a row's Organize sheet scrolls that row into view" which asserts scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' }) is called on the row when its Organize sheet opens.

rows.statement: After Resume all reopens only some sessions, it says how many reopened and why the rest stayed.
rows.threshold: the partial-resume status-line tests pass
rows.evidence: npx vitest run tests/ResumeBrowser-welcome-back.test.tsx (youcoded/desktop) — 19 passed, incl. 'a partial Resume press says how many reopened and that the rest need a model' and 'pluralizes the status line for more than one row left', which assert the partial-resume status line text.
